# HRangeSlider

> Two native range handles for choosing a bounded numeric interval.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.5.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HRangeSlider` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-range-slider>`.
- Constructor: `HearthRangeSliderElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HRangeSlider.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Added in v0.5.0. Two native range controls share a track and retain native keyboard stepping. Handles cannot cross; both remain separately keyboard-focusable at equal values.
- Model is [lower,upper]. FormData.getAll(name) returns two values in that order. Supply finite bounds and a positive step. Applications own unit conversion.

## Public API

modelValue, value: NumberRange · label, name, unit, lowerLabel, upperLabel: string · min, max, step: number · disabled: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    modelValue?: NumberRange;
    value?: NumberRange;
    label: string;
    name?: string;
    min?: number;
    max?: number;
    step?: number;
    unit?: string;
    disabled?: boolean;
    lowerLabel?: string;
    upperLabel?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{
    value: () => [0, 100],
    min: 0,
    max: 100,
    step: 1,
    unit: "",
    lowerLabel: "Minimum",
    upperLabel: "Maximum",
  }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(NumberRange), change(NumberRange)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        value: NumberRange
    ];
    change: [
        value: NumberRange
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, label, value, track, lower, upper

Use `hearth-range-slider::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export type NumberRange = [
    number,
    number
];
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HRangeSlider } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const capacity = ref<[number,number]>([20,80]);
</script>

<template>
  <HRangeSlider v-model="capacity" label="Capacity" name="capacity" unit="%" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-range-slider');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Capacity",
  "name": "capacity",
  "value": [
    20,
    80
  ],
  "unit": "%"
});

element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
